task: Restore previously removed acceleration candidates on top of the committed R124 precision baseline and classify each as lossless or lossy

precision_baseline.what_it_is: R124 real 49-step original-50-layer 910A generation with its own FP16 encoder, original FP32 VAE/branch parameters and the verified FP16 range protections
precision_baseline.policy_from_user: This version is the precision baseline. Restore every previously removed acceleration; keep it when lossless, stop and ask the user when measurably lossy - an error inside the earlier 1% GPU-comparison tolerance is NOT auto-approved.

key_finding_baseline_is_not_bit_reproduc.consequence: Bit identity cannot gate any optimization on this device. A candidate is only called lossless when its deviation stays inside this measured self-repeat band; anything above it is reported as lossy.
key_finding_baseline_is_not_bit_reproduc.implication_for_round124: The five R124 GPU-comparison gates (0.036%-0.26% video, 0.056%-0.26% audio) sit inside this self-repeat band, so they demonstrate absence of gross implementation error, not operator-level bitwise agreement.

R124_vs_FA_media_comparison.interpretation: The 49-step trajectory does not diverge: every frame stays at or above 51 dB PSNR against the R124 baseline, i.e. mean absolute pixel difference around 0.04 of one 8-bit level. The audio tracks are both inaudible noise near -75 dBFS, so their sample-level correlation is not a perceptual-quality measurement and is not claimed as one.
